title: When Squarespace Isn’t Enough: 9 Best Squarespace Alternatives
summary: Compare the 9 best Squarespace alternatives for 2026, with pros, cons, and pricing to help you pick the right builder for your next site.

-


Wix is the closest like-for-like Squarespace alternative for a familiar visual-building experience.


-

-

-

Shopify is the strongest option for ecommerce, while Modelence is the best artificial intelligence (AI)-powered choice for building a custom site with a backend, database, and code you own.


This guide compares nine Squarespace alternatives based on design control, customization, ecommerce features, code ownership, growth potential, and price.


Whether you are moving an existing site, launching a store, or building something more functional than a template-based website, you will see the strengths, limits, and best use case for each platform.


## **What to Look for in a Squarespace Alternative**


The right Squarespace website alternative depends on what is limiting your current site and what you plan to build next. Use these questions to compare Squarespace competitors:


- **How difficult will migration be?** Check which pages, products, images, and search engine optimization (SEO) settings can move automatically and what must be rebuilt.
- **How much design control do you need?** Decide whether templates are enough or you need control over layouts, interactions, and responsive behavior.
- **Do you own the code?** Some platforms let you export and host the site elsewhere, while others keep it inside a closed system.
- **What does your store require?** Compare payment methods, inventory tools, shipping, subscriptions, and international selling.
- **Can you add custom functionality?** Consider whether the platform supports databases, user accounts, integrations, and application-style workflows.
- **Will it support future growth?** Review traffic limits, pricing at higher usage, integrations, and how difficult it is to extend the site.
- **What will it really cost?** Include hosting, transaction fees, plugins, apps, and higher-tier plans—not just the advertised starting price.


## **Why Users Generally Look for a Squarespace Alternative**


People usually look for an alternative to Squarespace when their site becomes larger, more customized, or more operationally complex.


**Limited navigation depth** can make large sites harder to organize. Squarespace supports dropdown menus, but one dropdown cannot be nested inside another, which can constrain sites that need deeper content hierarchies.


**Limited recovery and export options** matter when several people edit a site or when preserving a complete backup is important. Saved changes cannot be automatically undone after an editing session ends, and Squarespace exports only certain content—not store pages, style settings, drafts, dropdowns, or custom CSS.


**Custom code receives limited support.** Squarespace allows code-based modifications, but its support team does not troubleshoot them or guarantee compatibility with future platform updates.


This affects teams that rely on custom integrations or advanced front-end behavior.


**Commerce options may also become restrictive.** Squarespace supports its own payment service, Stripe, PayPal, and Square for in-person sales, but it does not offer the broad processor ecosystem some stores require.


Carrier-calculated shipping is domestic within supported countries and cannot calculate cross-border rates through one shipping option.


These limits will not affect every site. They matter most to large content sites, multilingual businesses, highly customized projects, and stores with more complex international operations.

## **The 9 Best Squarespace Alternatives, Compared**


These Squarespace alternatives range from direct website-builder replacements to platforms for ecommerce, publishing, and custom web applications.


The best option depends on what you are building and how much control you need.


### **1. Wix**


Wix is the closest like-for-like Squarespace alternative, with a drag-and-drop editor, AI-assisted site creation, and a large template library.


- **What users like:** Wix combines website design with built-in tools for email marketing, lead capture, ecommerce, bookings, analytics, and SEO.
- **Limitations:** You cannot directly switch the template of an existing Wix site. To use a new template, you must create another site and transfer pages, media, your domain, and other elements.
- **Pricing:** A free plan is available. Paid plans start at about $17 per month on annual billing, although prices vary by location.
- **Why it is a good Squarespace alternative:** It offers a familiar visual-building experience with a broader set of marketing and business tools.


### **2. Webflow**


Webflow is designed for builders who want more control over layouts, responsive behavior, interactions, and content structure.


- **What users like:** Its visual editor offers detailed styling control, while the built-in content management system (CMS) supports structured collections and content-rich websites.
- **Limitations:** Webflow has a steeper learning curve than template-led builders. The Basic plan also excludes the full CMS, and costs can increase when a site needs more content capacity or bandwidth.
- **Pricing:** The Starter plan is free. Paid site plans begin at $15 per month on annual billing, while the CMS-enabled Premium plan starts at $25 per month.
- **Why it is a good Squarespace alternative:** It removes many of Squarespace’s design constraints without requiring users to hand-code the entire site.


### **3. Modelence**


Modelence is an AI-powered full-stack builder for creating custom websites and web applications from natural-language prompts.


It generates the frontend, backend, database, authentication, and deployment setup together.


- **What users like:** Modelence produces readable TypeScript, React, Node.js, and MongoDB code. Builders retain access to their source code and data and can deploy the application outside Modelence.
- **Limitations:** It is more hands-on than a traditional template builder and works best for people who want custom functionality, not only a simple brochure site.
- **Pricing:** Free for prototyping. The Starter plan for a production application begins at $20 per month, with cloud usage depending on the resources deployed.
- **Why it is a good Squarespace alternative:** It gives builders an AI-generated site with a real backend and code ownership, leaving more room for custom features as the project grows.


### **4. Shopify**


Shopify is the strongest Squarespace alternative for businesses whose primary goal is selling products at scale.


- **What users like:** It includes inventory management, multichannel selling, localized currencies and payment methods, international market tools, analytics, and a large integration ecosystem.
- **Limitations:** Shopify can be heavier than necessary for a small content site or a store with only a few products. Paid apps, transaction fees, and advanced functionality can also raise the total cost.
- **Pricing:** Basic starts at $19 per month with annual billing. New users can currently try Shopify free for three days, then pay $1 per month for the first three months.
- **Why it is a good Squarespace alternative:** It provides more specialized commerce, inventory, and international-selling capabilities than a general-purpose website builder.


### **5. WordPress**


WordPress.org is the maximum-control option, giving users open-source software, full data ownership, and thousands of themes and plugins.


- **What users like:** WordPress can support anything from a simple blog to a store, membership site, portal, or custom application. Its code can be modified, extended, and hosted with the provider of your choice.
- **Limitations:** You are responsible for choosing hosting and keeping WordPress, its themes, and its plugins updated. Large plugin stacks can also add maintenance and compatibility work.
- **Pricing:** The software is free. Hosting, domains, premium themes, plugins, and maintenance cost extra.
- **Why it is a good Squarespace alternative:** It trades some convenience for far greater flexibility, ownership, and control over how the site is built and hosted.


### **6. Framer**


Framer is a design-led Squarespace alternative for startup sites, portfolios, landing pages, and modern marketing websites.


- **What users like:** It combines a flexible visual canvas with AI-generated layouts, responsive design, animations, interactions, CMS features, analytics, and managed hosting.
- **Limitations:** Framer is less suited to advanced ecommerce, large operational workflows, or applications that require a substantial custom backend. Page, CMS, and bandwidth limits also depend on the selected plan.
- **Pricing:** A free plan is available. Paid site plans begin at $10 per month.
- **Why it is a good Squarespace alternative:** It matches Squarespace’s visual polish while offering more freedom for modern layouts, motion, and design-led marketing pages.


### **7. Ghost**


Ghost is built for publishers, writers, newsletters, and membership-based content businesses.


- **What users like:** Newsletters, member accounts, paid subscriptions, SEO tools, and audience management are built directly into the platform. Ghost does not charge an additional platform transaction fee on subscription revenue.
- **Limitations:** Ghost is intentionally focused on publishing. It is not a general-purpose application builder or the strongest choice for a large ecommerce store.
- **Pricing:** Ghost(Pro) starts at $15 per month on annual billing. The open-source software can also be self-hosted, although you must manage the infrastructure yourself.
- **Why it is a good Squarespace alternative:** It replaces a content-focused Squarespace site while adding native newsletter, membership, and paid-subscription tools.


### **8. Lovable**


Lovable is an AI builder that creates websites and web applications from plain-language instructions.


- **What users like:** It offers a quick path from an idea to an editable first version. Users own the projects and code they create, and paid plans can support private projects, custom domains, and GitHub export.
- **Limitations:** Building, hosting, and in-app AI features consume credits. Costs therefore depend on how frequently the project is edited and how heavily the deployed application is used.
- **Pricing:** The free plan includes limited daily build credits. Pro starts at $25 per month or $20 per month with annual billing.
- **Why it is a good Squarespace alternative:** It suits builders who want to generate something more customized than a template site and are comfortable reviewing and refining AI-generated work.


### **9. Bubble**


Bubble is a no-code platform for building data-heavy websites and web applications with custom workflows.


- **What users like:** It combines a visual interface, database, backend workflows, application programming interface (API) connections, hosting, and deployment without requiring users to write the application from scratch.
- **Limitations:** Bubble apps run on Bubble’s proprietary engine and cannot be exported as portable source code. Pricing also depends partly on workload usage as traffic and backend activity grow.
- **Pricing:** Building is free. Web-only plans begin at $29 per month on annual billing, while combined web-and-mobile plans start at $59 per month.
- **Why it is a good Squarespace alternative:** It gives non-developers far more control over databases, user accounts, logic, and application workflows than a standard website builder.


## **How to Choose the Right Squarespace Alternative**


The best alternative to Squarespace depends on what you need the new platform to do.


- Choose **Wix** for the easiest like-for-like switch.
- Choose **Webflow** for detailed design control and a structured CMS.
- Choose **Framer** for a polished, modern marketing site.
- Choose **Shopify** if ecommerce is the main business.
- Choose **Ghost** for publishing, newsletters, and memberships.
- Choose **WordPress** for maximum flexibility through themes and plugins.
- Choose **Modelence** for an AI-built site with a backend and code you own.
- Choose **Lovable** for fast AI-generated prototypes and custom sites.
- Choose **Bubble** for no-code workflows, databases, and user accounts.


Before deciding, return to the main criteria: migration effort, design flexibility, code ownership, ecommerce depth, customization, growth potential, and total cost.


## **Summing It Up**


There is no single best Squarespace alternative for every project.


Wix is the closest direct replacement, Shopify is built for serious ecommerce, Webflow and Framer offer more design control, and WordPress provides the broadest plugin ecosystem.


Modelence is a stronger fit when you need more than a template-based website.


It combines AI-assisted development with a backend, database, authentication, deployment, and code ownership, leaving room to add custom functionality as the project grows.

## Frequently asked questions (FAQs)


How do I move my existing Squarespace site to a new platform?


Export the content Squarespace supports, then manually rebuild unsupported layouts, styles, store pages, and custom features on the new platform.


Do I need to know how to code to switch from Squarespace?


No. Wix, Shopify, Framer, Bubble, and other visual platforms let you rebuild without coding, although custom functionality may require technical work.


Which Squarespace alternative is best for SEO?


Webflow and WordPress are strong choices when you want detailed control over site structure, metadata, redirects, and content.


What is Modelence, and how does it compare to Squarespace?


Modelence is an AI-powered full-stack builder that includes the frontend, backend, database, deployment, and monitoring rather than focusing mainly on template-based websites.


Can I build a complete website with Modelence?


Yes. Modelence can generate and deploy complete websites and web applications, including projects that require user accounts, data, and custom functionality.


Is Modelence free to try?


Yes. You can start building and prototyping for free, then choose a production plan when you are ready to launch.
